verdict.rationale: Steel publishes source in a public GitHub repo (steel-dev/steel-browser) that describes itself as an open-source browser API, which the docs and an HN commenter echo, so the core of the story is supported. The evidence never names the license, and it does not show whether the managed-cloud features (stealth, CAPTCHA solving, managed proxies, agent traces) are in the open repo or proprietary. Coverage is therefore partial. missing for 10: an explicitly named open license (e.g., Apache/MIT text or a LICENSE reference), evidence that the full product including cloud features is open source rather than only the core browser API, independent hands-on confirmation of self-hosting from source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
